description: INFER MEANING FROM CONTEXT for an OUT-OF-VOCABULARY filler, the FORWARD twin of reading_review's selectional-incoherence scorer -- as a GRAPH JOIN, not a Python membership test. `SelectionalClassPair` is the scalar-row normal form of one (verb_class -> requires_class) admission: 'a verb.emotion relation admits a noun.person subject' is ONE row, 'admits a noun.animal subject' is ANOTHER, so the rule below JOINS a PredicationSlot to a SelectionalClassPair by Eq(verb_class) AND Eq(slot) -- the graph join that replaces `if rel_class in verb_classes`. This is independent seed data (own node type) alongside reading_review's existing list-valued `SelectionalRestriction` -- that node type keeps its own shape untouched (its consumer, reading_review._predication_selectional_incoherence, is not touched by this seed). domains/meaning_inference.py's Python side is PURE ANNOTATION: for every grounded predication argument it writes `oov`/`is_pronoun` facts on the filler Concept (WordNet/closed-class reads -- capability, not decision) and an UNCONDITIONAL `PredicationSlot{slot, rel_verb_class, relation}` node (rel_verb_class is simply null for a non-verb relation like 'of' -- Python does not branch on that, the null just never joins). Three rules make the WHOLE decision, in Rust: `infer_sense_mint`/`infer_sense_combine` perform the join (gated on oov + not-pronoun + not-already-genuinely-grounded) and mint-or-raise-confidence an `InferredSense{term, sense_class, confidence, via, source, status, revisable}` per (term, sense_class) -- the SAME ReadingBelief shape reading_collapse._record_reading_belief already uses for the passive/stative collapse (idempotent; a later grounding supersedes it in ONE set_attr, `infer_sense_supersede`). `grounded` is a flag any grounding process (teach(), a future ground_unknowns pass, ...) may set on a Concept; this seed only reacts to it -- the placeholder Concept `_write_predications` mints for EVERY predication argument, known or not, never carries it, so it never falsely counts as 'known'. SLICE 2 adds DEFINITIONAL inference: an UNCONDITIONAL `Predication{relation, subj_name, genus_full, genus_head, subj_oov, genus_head_grounded, genus_head_class}` fact node -- written for EVERY predication with an object, pairing SUBJECT and OBJECT within one predication instance (the pairing PredicationSlot, one-argument-per-node, cannot express) -- feeds `infer_sense_from_definition`: an is_a predication (`Eq(relation,'is_a')` -- the RELATION SELECTION, a rule Eq, never a Python branch) whose subject is OOV and whose object's GENUS HEAD is grounded mints a HIGHER-confidence `InferredSense{source:'definition'}` straight from the in-situ definition ('A glimt is a lake.' -> glimt:noun.object via 'lake'; 'A florbin is a small bird.' -> florbin:noun.animal via genus_head 'bird'). Coexists with a selectional-sourced row for the same term as a separate, higher-confidence row -- no forced supersede between sources. SLICE 3 adds MORPHOLOGICAL inference: an OOV term's own SHAPE (not its syntactic context) carries a semantic class -- 'florbitis' names a disease STATE by the '-itis' suffix alone, with no verb or copula to lean on. `MorphemeClass{affix, position, sense_class, weight, affix_len, note}` is the scalar-row codebook (one row per (affix, position) admission, the SAME normal form as SelectionalClassPair); domains/meaning_inference.py writes an UNCONDITIONAL `AffixCandidate{affix, position, term, affix_len}` per every 2..6-char suffix and 2..4-char prefix of an OOV content-word filler's head (mechanical `str` slicing -- every candidate substring is emitted, none preferred) linked `agent -has_affix_candidate-> ac -affix_fills-> filler_concept` (a DEDICATED edge type, not `PredicationSlot`'s `fills` -- a Concept can hold many AffixCandidate in-edges at once, and the daemon's documented run_rules gotcha is 'two same-type incoming edges on one node can break matching for that edge type', so morphology gets its own edge type rather than risk sharing PredicationSlot's). `infer_sense_from_morphology` JOINS AffixCandidate to MorphemeClass by Eq(affix) AND Eq(position) -- the graph join that decides which slice of the word means something, gated on the SAME oov + not-pronoun + not-already-grounded guards slice 1 uses, deduped per (term, sense_class, source='morphology'). Weight is 0.45 -- BELOW selectional (0.6) and definition (0.9): shape-only evidence is the WEAKEST source, context beats bare morphology when both are present. AMBIGUOUS overlapping affixes of the SAME sense_class (e.g. '-ectomy' and its own tail '-tomy', both noun.act) resolve via an explicit LONGEST-MATCH guard: the rule abstains on a shorter same-class match when a longer same-class MorphemeClass ALSO matches an AffixCandidate on the same filler (a nested Exists/InNeighbours check over `affix_len`, a static per-row field -- not a Python decision). Affixes of DIFFERENT sense_class are never suppressed -- they coexist as separate rows, exactly like slice 1's multi-class admission. '-ium' is deliberately NOT seeded (reserved to demonstrate teach()-grown element/metal coverage via '-onium' -- the morphology-slice twin of slice 1's taught verb.motion coverage). SLICE 4 adds ANALOGY inference: the SAME unconditional Predication{relation,...} fact slice 2 already writes for every predication with an object ALSO carries relation=='similar' for an explicit comparison ('A glorb is like a pump.'/'A florx resembles a bird.' -- the reader's own comparative_like_cop/comparative_like constructions), so `infer_sense_from_analogy` needs NO adapter change at all: it is `infer_sense_from_definition`'s exact JOIN shape with ONE Eq swapped (Eq(relation,'similar') instead of Eq(relation,'is_a')) -- an OOV subject of an explicit-comparison predication whose compared-to OBJECT grounds mints InferredSense{source:'analogy', sense_class:genus_head_class, via:genus_head, confidence:0.7} -- BELOW a copular identity definition (0.9, 'A glimt IS a lake' asserts identity) but ABOVE mere selectional admission (0.6, a verb class merely ADMITS a filler): an authored simile is stronger evidence than a class-only admission, weaker than an assertion of identity. Coexists with definition/selectional/morphology rows for the same term as separate rows -- confidence orders them, no forced supersede. SLICE 4 STRETCH adds STRUCTURAL analogy (no explicit like/resembles cue): domains/meaning_inference.py's `annotate_relational_signatures` re-aggregates the ALREADY-WRITTEN PredicationSlot facts into `own_relations` (a term's own (slot, relation) subject-participation history) on every filler Concept, and holds a DEDICATED `ConceptSignature{name, signature, concept}` codebook entry per GROUNDED filler (its own relational profile + its held WordNet class) -- a codebook_type='ConceptSignature' distinct from the composer's own 'ShapeSignature' codebook, so ShapeDecode never cross-contaminates the two. `infer_sense_from_structural_analogy` decodes an OOV term's own multi-relation profile (>=2 distinct subject-relations, Gte(Count(...),2)) against that codebook via the held ShapeDecode Term; when exactly ONE grounded concept's signature FULLY explains it (empty residual AND a single-part plan -- Count(plan)==1, so the class is never a composed blend across multiple sources), that concept's class transfers, mined via DictGet/IndexAt on the SAME decode. Confidence 0.5: weaker than an authored simile (0.7, an explicit claim) and selectional admission (0.6, a coarse verb-class filter), but real, non-fabricated multi-relation structural evidence, so above bare morphology (0.45, shape alone).

microtheory.name: meaning_inference
microtheory.description: an OOV filler in a selectionally-restricted slot gets a provisional, revisable semantic type inferred from a held (verb_class -> requires_class) join, never a Python membership test

attrs.note: a verb.cognition relation (thinks/believes/knows/...) admits a noun.person subject.
a verb.cognition relation also admits a noun.animal subject.
a verb.emotion relation (fears/loves/dreads/...) admits a noun.person subject.
a verb.emotion relation also admits a noun.animal subject.
-itis names an inflammation/disease STATE (arthritis, bronchitis, appendicitis).
-ase names an ENZYME substance (protease, lactase, amylase).
-ectomy names the surgical ACT of removal (appendectomy, tonsillectomy).

-tomy names the surgical ACT of cutting (tracheotomy, lobotomy) -- its tail overlaps -ectomy's; same sense_class, so the longest-match guard prefers -ectomy when both match one word, rather than minting a duplicate row.
-ology names a FIELD OF STUDY (biology, geology) -- a cognition/knowledge-domain noun.
un- negates the base (unhappy, unknown) -- a negation modifier, not a noun class.
non- negates the base (nonexistent, nonstarter) -- same negation class as un-.
